title: `AppendCheckpointTrailer` can emit a trailer the final-block parser (and git) reject

verdict.rationale: The evidence covers moving and tightening the trailer heuristic, but nothing shows anyone chose for the writer to treat indented trailer-shaped lines as a trailer block. The writer's looser TrimSpace grammar appears to be an unconsidered divergence from the reader and git, not a deliberate choice.

- Offer to amend the last commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer
- Support --force flag for non-interactive use
- Depth-limited directory walking for transcript search fallback

Extract canPromptInteractively to shared interactive package

The cli and strategy packages each carried a private copy of
canPromptInteractively() with identical TTY-detection and
ENTIRE_TEST_TTY override semantics. strategy cannot import cli (import
cycle), so duplication was previously the cheap workaround — but it
means the two copies silently drift apart on every refactor.

Extract the shared helper to a new leaf package cmd/entire/cli/
interactive, which depends only on os. Both cli (attach, explain
summary provider, login, setup) and strategy (manual_commit_rewind)
now import and call interactive.CanPromptInteractively().

Test coverage moved from setup_test.go (which tested the cli copy) to
interactive/interactive_test.go, preserving the three env-var scenarios
(forced on, forced off, non-"1" value).

Isolated package with no cli/strategy dependencies means future shared
TTY/interactivity helpers (such as the duplicated isAccessibleMode)
have an obvious home when the scope is right.
